answer: Peer-prediction scoring resists sybils. Each key locks a slashable marble deposit and commits a private forecast of a public random event into a public orchard of sealed reports. When a later tide reveals the outcome, each report is scored against a random peer sample; near-duplicate forecasts from supposedly independent keys are treated as one operator, and every linked marble is slashed. Copying one model forms a tight cluster and burns the stake. Looking independent requires N distinct models and N deposits held through the scoring tide, so compute and capital scale with farm size.
